item.text: {"question_id":"3B.8","answer":"In 2023, peaceful protest, dissent, and organization received formal but inconsistently applied protection. The constitution provided for peaceful assembly and association, and a presidential electoral-security directive instructed state institutions to protect voters and electoral participation and to sanction violence and discrimination, but the evidence does not show that these commitments reliably protected protest or ensured remedy (BATCH-0011-E011; BATCH-0009-E001). Authorities used advance-notification and authorization rules to restrict opposition and civil-society protests, especially in eastern provinces and state-of-siege areas; police blocked opposition gatherings, used tear gas and beatings, and detained demonstrators. The May 20 march produced at least 30 serious injuries and arrests, while three officers were detained, with proceedings still pending (BATCH-0011-E011; BATCH-0002-E011; BATCH-0003-E004). The August 30 Goma operation was substantially more severe: authorities had banned the protest, deployed army and police under operational plans, and security forces killed at least 56 people according to the official count, injured more than 80, and arrested more than 150; Amnesty’s investigation found deliberate killings of unarmed protesters and identified command-level responsibility allegations. Six officers were tried and four convicted, but Amnesty characterized the investigation and justice process as incomplete, while authorities also collectively prosecuted protesters (BATCH-0011-E018). Dissent and organization were further constrained by arrests and prosecutions of critics and journalists under defamation, false-information, press, and digital-code provisions; Bujakera remained in pretrial detention in September 2023, and journalists reported intimidation and self-censorship (BATCH-0011-E011; BATCH-0025-E012). These adverse patterns were not universal: police escorted a peaceful Goma march in October and officials received its memorandum, and government assistance took an attacked journalist to hospital, although accountability for party-supporter attacks was unresolved (BATCH-0022-E014; BATCH-0027-E002). Attribution to Tshisekedi is strongest for the national legal/security framework and his public praise of the police chief after the May crackdown; the supplied evidence does not establish that he personally ordered every local restriction or the Goma killings. Overall, the evidence supports recurring and, in Goma, severe state interference with peaceful assembly and dissent, with some investigations and convictions but incomplete and contested remedy.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0003-E004","BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0025-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0027-E002","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0002-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence is concentrated in 2023 incidents and does not establish how consistently other protests were protected.","Goma casualty figures are disputed: the official count was at least 56, while Amnesty reported a confidential UN estimate of 102 deaths.","The supplied evidence does not establish a direct presidential order for every restriction or for the Goma killings; provincial, military, police, and party-supporter responsibility must be distinguished.","The legality and proportionality of particular restrictions and the factual merits of the charges against Bujakera are not fully resolved.","Investigations, trials, and convictions provide some accountability evidence, but the completeness, independence, finality, and victim remedy of those processes remain limited or contested."] ,"corrections_made":["Removed unsupported references to a 2023 electoral-security directive as direct protection of protest; the supplied directive concerns electoral materials, voters, violence, discrimination, and electoral security.","Removed unsupported claims that authorities eased the state of siege or that journalists broadly faced disappearances and attacks by ruling-party supporters; retained only supplied, question-relevant evidence.","Corrected the Goma description to preserve the disputed casualty figures, the planned operation, the army-police deployment, the convictions, the incomplete justice process, and collective prosecution of protesters.","Added the constitutional and association protections, authorization barriers, state-of-siege restrictions, journalist criminalization, October peaceful police escort, and unresolved accountability for party-supporter attacks.","Narrowed presidential attribution to the supplied evidence: the legal/security framework and praise of the police chief, not every local incident or the Goma killings."] ,"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A full ledger review could determine whether additional 2023 evidence establishes the consistency of protest protection, the legal status and enforcement of the state of siege, or stronger evidence of presidential command, tolerance, or remedy.","The Goma casualty discrepancy and the final status of military prosecutions could materially affect the severity and accountability assessment."]}
